$description: Websites (issue 53): a fluid display scale for site headings, section rhythm and site widths. Sizes grow with the window between a 360 phone and a 1280 desktop, from the phone size of an M3 role to the desktop size of the next one up. App type is not touched: apps keep the fixed M3 roles.

font.$description: The display face (follows the display dial).

size.$description: One h1 per page: display-small (36) on a phone to display-large (57) from 1280.

tracking.$description: Follows display-large, so another display face drops Inter's tracking.

size.$description: Section titles (h2): headline-medium (28) on a phone to display-medium (45) from 1280.
The paragraph under a hero or section title: 17 on a phone to title-large (22) from 1280.

section-space.$description: Space between two sections (padding at the top and bottom of each): 64 on a phone to 112 from 1280.

section-space-compact.$description: The phone end of section-space; for a tight band (an announcement, a logo row).

section-gap.$description: Inside a section: between its heading block and its content. 32 on a phone to 56 from 1280.

margin.$description: Side margin of a site page: 16 on a phone (as apps) to 32 from 1280.

section-space-roomy.$description: section-space under data-density="roomy": 80 on a phone to 144 from 1280.

section-gap-roomy.$description: section-gap under data-density="roomy": 40 on a phone to 72 from 1280.

margin-roomy.$description: margin under data-density="roomy": 20 on a phone to 40 from 1280 (the roomy layout margins).

width.$description: Site content width (1200): sections, header and footer line up on it.

measure.$description: Line length of a lead or section intro (about 60 characters at lead size).

measure-wide.$description: Wide measure: a centered hero or section heading block.
